comments.note: Removed stale WP build-plan inline comments from src/index.ts (e.g. '// Engine exports (WP-002)', '// Loader exports (WP-003)', 'Feature modules will be exported here as they are implemented in subsequent WPs.'). These are internal task-tracker artefacts that have no place in a published library barrel — they confuse external contributors and falsely imply the API is incomplete. Also trimmed the module-level JSDoc to the clean single-sentence form. Behaviour is entirely unchanged.

src/utils/regex.ts — implementation is exemplary: standard TC39 special-character set, full JSDoc with @param/@returns/@example (including a real-world usage example showing the Markdown-table pattern), pure-function annotation in the file-level comment, and correct ESM .js extension on the barrel import.

src/utils/index.ts — uses a named re-export ('export { escapeRegExp }') rather than a glob re-export ('export *'). This is slightly more explicit about the public surface and is a good pattern for a utility barrel, since it prevents accidental leakage if regex.ts later gains unexported helpers that are then made exportable by mistake.

src/plugins/ledger/role-validator.ts — the escapeRegExp call in validateNoteOnlyGuard (line 114) is correctly placed: entry.tool is escaped before being interpolated into new RegExp(...). This is the exact use-case the utility was extracted for and confirms the extraction rationale is sound.

[documentation-forward] src/utils/index.ts has no module-level JSDoc comment (only regex.ts and role-validator.ts have them). Consider adding a brief module docstring consistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase — e.g. '/** src/utils/index.ts — Barrel re-export for shared utility modules. */'.
